clue.text: Prison shops renovated with commercial support

indicators.note: something renovated is done over and rebuilt, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Jail shops get a makeover paid for by a business backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges PRISON SHOPS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsorship is backing, usually money, given by a company in return for publicity.

clue.text: 15 people claim ginseng mostly damaging

definitions.note: refers to 15 across, HUMP, as in a speed hump in the road

indicators.note: damaging something knocks it out of shape, so the pooled letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word ginseng is kept

explanation.surface: Some people say ginseng is mostly harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims GINSENG to GINSEN; 'damaging' then shuffles PEOPLE CLAIM GINSEN into SLEEPING POLICEMAN, the British name for a speed bump laid across a road to slow traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping policeman is British slang for a speed hump, a raised strip that forces drivers to slow.

clue.text: Procedure to imagine earth facing 18

definitions.note: 18 is BACK (18 across); the answer means facing, and, as front is to back, the contrary of it

parts.note: an operation in surgery is a procedure, OP for short
to posit is to suppose or imagine something as a premise

explanation.surface: A method for picturing the planet turned towards the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 points to the answer at 18 across, BACK; the definition plays on 'facing' and on the answer as the contrary of back.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means situated across from and facing something, and also means contrary, as front is to back.

clue.text: Pervert loves crack

indicators.note: to pervert something is to twist it from its proper form, so the letters of loves are twisted

explanation.surface: A deviant's affections break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' reads as a noun but is a verb telling you to rearrange LOVES.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or a code is to solve it, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Prepared to access data on roadside bomb

parts.note: a computer reads data when it accesses it
IED, improvised explosive device, the usual term for a roadside bomb

explanation.surface: Getting ready to download information about a bomb by the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'access data' is computing language for reading a file; IED stands for improvised explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: Readied means made ready, a direct synonym of prepared.

clue.text: Monopolise pictures by church's last engraver

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to yourself, to monopolise it
art, collectively, means pictures

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word church

explanation.surface: Someone hogging the paintings next to the end of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver, known for series such as 'A Rake's Progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is best known for his satirical engravings, so he is an example of an engraver.

clue.text: See 1
Stole yacht for one missing 18

indicators.note: 18 is BACK, so 'missing back' tells you the rear letter of the word for the vessel is lost

parts.note: a yacht is an example of a boat; 'for one' marks the example

explanation.surface: A scarf left on a yacht that has lost its stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is BACK, so 'missing 18' means missing its back letter. 'Stole' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long feathery or fur scarf, a kind of stole worn round the shoulders.

clue.text: Game, though 15 18 is not a variation

definitions.text: Game, though 15 18 is not a variation

parts.words: Game, though 15 18 is not a variation
parts.note: 15 18 is HUMP BACK: a humpback is a kind of road crossing over a river, but there is no humpback version of the card game of the same name

explanation.surface: A card game, but humpback is not one of its variants.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the card game, and a humpback bridge, sharply arched in the middle, is a variety of the structure but not of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players, and also a structure spanning a gap, of which humpback is one type.

clue.text: Flies when keeping President concealed

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the word for when goes round the other pieces

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: Someone flees while keeping a president hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like a verb but is the plural noun: greenfly and blackfly are aphids.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are tiny sap-sucking insects commonly called greenfly or blackfly, so they are flies in name.

clue.text: Get rid of former footballer (not European)

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: not tells you a letter is to be left out of the footballer's name

parts.note: Pelé, the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: Dropping an ex-footballer, who wasn't from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelé has two Es; dropping the final one leaves PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or force someone to leave, so to get rid of them.

clue.text: Swimmer needs a fleshing out

indicators.note: out here means out of order or put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer needs to bulk up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleshing out' reads as a phrase meaning filling out, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on A FLESHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An angelfish is a tropical fish, and fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: 18 side of resort featured in advert

definitions.note: 18 is BACK, so the definition reads back side, the bottom

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the resort's name goes inside the word for the advert

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian resort

explanation.surface: An advert for the seaside side of a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is BACK, so '18 side' is backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior as a noun is a humorous word for the buttocks, a person's backside.

clue.text: Imprisoned old Conservative leader first

indicators.note: first places the letter ahead of the other piece
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Conservative

parts.note: aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly Tory party chief put first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the leading letter of Conservative goes in front of AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Caged means shut in a cage, so confined, imprisoned.

clue.text: Father invested in famous small computer

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the word for father goes inside the word for famous

parts.note: noted means well known, famous
Pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Dad has put money into a well-known small computer firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance in the surface but is a container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a small portable computer, a term once used for compact laptops.

clue.text: Location city is under pressure to fix permanently

indicators.note: in a down clue being under means coming below, so the city follows pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
LA, Los Angeles, is a city
to cement something is to fix it firmly in place

explanation.surface: A city under pressure to settle something for good.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is under' puts LA below P.
explanation.definitionFit: Placement is the act of putting something in position, or its location.

clue.text: Smell beginning to permeate swelling

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of permeate

explanation.surface: A smell starts to spread through a swollen place.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British informal for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hump is a rounded lump or bump, such as a swelling on the back.

clue.text: Can name the Spanish castle in Cornwall

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tag is a name or label
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Can the Spaniards name the castle in Cornwall?
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintagel is a ruined castle on the Cornish coast linked in legend to King Arthur.

clue.text: Way to restrain listener fighting to the 18

definitions.note: 18 is BACK, so this reads to the back

indicators.note: restraining holds something in, so the road abbreviation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the ear is the organ of listening
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A route to hold back someone overhearing a battle at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is BACK, so the definition is 'to the back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearward means towards the rear, so to the back.

clue.text: Second lawyer sailor rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned away, refused, so the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: KC, King's Counsel, is a senior British barrister
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A second lawyer turns down a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is a verb here, as when you second a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it, giving formal support.

clue.text: Steals away, sleeps around and gets up

indicators.note: around means the word for sleeps goes round the other piece

parts.note: kips means sleeps, informally

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means rising, so the letters of and are read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off, sleeps around and rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' reads the word and upwards as DNA; 'around' wraps the sleep word round it. 'sleeps around' looks like a phrase in the surface but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to carry someone away illegally, so to steal them away.

clue.text: Duration of program revises UN remit

indicators.note: revising something reworks it, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The United Nations reworks its mandate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revises' rearranges UN REMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Run time is how long a computer program or film lasts when it is played.

clue.text: Design change for remainder probably all achievable in the end

parts.note: the rest is what remains, the remainder

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A redesign for the rest is likely to be doable in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' takes the last letters of probably, all and achievable: Y, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle is to give something a new style, a change in its design.

clue.text: Journalist in his element up country

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in means the editor goes inside the word for news

parts.note: a journalist's element, where he is at home, is the news
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter in his element up in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives NEDEWS, which 'up' reads from the bottom of the down entry upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, a country.

clue.text: Plan amateur dismissed

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur
out means dismissed, as a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A plan that saw the amateur sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is the arrangement or plan of a page, garden or building.

clue.text: Viewing essentially healthy 15 18?

definitions.note: 15 18 is HUMP BACK; the question mark says this is an example, a humpback

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the middle letter, of the word viewing

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Is watching basically healthy for a hunchback?
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the central letter W of VIEWING; 15 18 is humpback.
explanation.definitionFit: A humpback is a large baleen species of whale, so the answer is the animal it is an example of.

clue.text: One who's got the 15 enchanted rides unsteadily round

definitions.note: 15 is HUMP; to have the hump is British slang for being sulky or disgruntled

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the word for enchanted
moving unsteadily means wobbling about, so the letters of rides are jumbled

parts.note: sent means thrilled or enchanted, as in 'the music sent me'

explanation.surface: A grumpy person, delighted, takes wobbly rides around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' gives DISER, which 'round' wraps round the middle piece. To 'have the hump' is British slang for being annoyed or sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter disagrees with the prevailing view, so stretches to one who is disgruntled, one with the hump.

clue.text: Gets rid of defaulting Republican and relaxes

indicators.note: defaulting means failing to turn up, so the Republican letter is absent from the word

parts.note: erases means removes, gets rid of

explanation.surface: A defaulting Republican is dropped, and things calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaulting' removes the R from ERASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eases means lessens tension or slackens, a synonym of relaxes.

clue.text: Dryad getting lost around capital is one with the 15

definitions.note: 15 is HUMP, so this is an animal with a hump

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the capital's name
getting lost suggests going astray, so the letters of dryad are scrambled

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A wood nymph lost her way around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting lost' gives D...DARY split round the capital, which 'around' signals. 'One' also hints at the single hump.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromedary is the Arabian camel, which has a single hump on its back.

clue.text: Character originally seen in Grease makes album

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A character who first appeared in the musical Grease records an album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of seen in Grease makes album.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Head Brazil?

definitions.meaning: the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Is the head of state from Brazil?
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, and a Brazil nut is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Bits of vegetables fraudulently sold as dates

indicators.note: something done fraudulently is rigged or faked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pieces of vegetables dishonestly passed off as dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fraudulently' rearranges SOLD AS DATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A tossed salad is mixed pieces of raw vegetables and leaves tossed in dressing.
